---
title: "Figure 6B — the decision, against a number you can measure: distortion (size and shape) versus the memory left in the least-squares residual"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
WHAT THIS IS, and why it closes the paper. Every other figure in this set is indexed by the DESIGN
(channel count, noise, sampling interval). This one is indexed by a number the reader MEASURES on
their own record, with no model, no derivative and no fit: the integrated autocorrelation of the
standardized residual of a least-squares fit, tau_int, in normalized Sokal / Kish form, null 1 for a
white residual. It counts how many intervals the likelihood effectively has for every interval it
believes it has.

So the reader's procedure is: fit by least squares, which they were going to do anyway; compute
tau_int from the residual, which costs nothing; find their x on this panel; read what least squares
is doing to their error bars, and what the boundary-conditioned filter would do instead. The vertical
distance between the two series at their x IS what switching buys them.

EVERY MARK IS ONE CELL OF THE DESIGN GRID AND ONE BATTERY OF 10 000 SIMULATIONS. There is no binning
here: an earlier draft binned in tau_int and the binning manufactured a non-monotone median by mixing
cells that differ in sampling interval, which is exactly the structure this panel exists to show.

HOW A MARK ENCODES BOTH NUMBERS. The distortion of a member is not one number, it is a size and a
shape: m = exp(mean log lambda) is the typical factor by which the reported information is wrong, and
a = exp(sd log lambda) is how much that factor VARIES from parameter direction to parameter
direction. A mark is therefore a point at m with a bar from m/a to m*a, which is the actual range of
per-direction factors. On log axes the bar is symmetric about the point, which is why the axes are
log and why the shape is written as a multiplicative spread and not as a plus-or-minus.

Read the bar's ENDS, not only its centre: the lower end is the reader's best-determined direction and
the upper end their worst. A mark centred at 6 with a bar from 1.9 to 19.5 says that even the
best-determined parameter is off by a factor 2 and the worst by 20.

IN ERROR-BAR UNITS, take the square root: the distortion is a ratio of informations, so a distortion
of 1.15 is a 7 per cent error on a confidence interval and nobody should care, 2 is 41 per cent, and
4 is a factor two, which turns a nominal 95 per cent interval into about 68. The panel deliberately
draws NO threshold. The criterion belongs to the reader and the axis lets them place it.

WHAT THE PANEL SHOWS, measured.

  (1) N_ch and noise DROP OUT. At matched tau_int the least-squares size agrees to three digits over
      four decades of channel count: at tau_int ~ 1.04 it reads 1.127, 1.135, 1.123, 1.145 for N_ch
      10, 100, 1000, 10000; at 1.21 it reads 2.198, 2.163, 2.211, 2.162. The two design variables
      that look like they should matter enter ONLY through the measured statistic.

  (2) THE SAMPLING INTERVAL DOES NOT, which is why the marks are coloured by it. At tau_int ~ 2.87
      with interval 0.01 the size is 8.9; at tau_int ~ 2.6 to 3.0 with interval 0.5 it is 1.56 to
      1.63, a factor 5.7 apart at the same measured memory. Within one interval the collapse is again
      exact: the whole interval-0.5 group sits between 1.56 and 1.63 across noise 0.1 to 1000 and
      N_ch 1000 to 10000. So the reader needs TWO numbers, and they have both: the one they measure
      and the one they chose when they set the sampling rate.

  (3) THE SHAPE SATURATES. Least squares' bar stops growing in height at about x3.3 from tau_int ~ 9
      onward while its centre keeps climbing from 6 to 53. Consequence, and it corrects a looser
      statement made earlier in the project: an effective-N rescaling DOES capture the part that
      keeps growing. What it never captures is a fixed x3.3 spread across directions, which stays
      whatever the memory does.

  (4) THE FILTER IS FLAT. IR sits at 1.00 in size and at 1.04 in shape at every x, and 1.043 +- 0.010
      is the estimation floor of this statistic, so those bars are measuring the bootstrap and not a
      distortion. The independent variable sweeps a factor of 20 and the filter does not move. The
      only departures are at N_ch = 10.

  (5) ONE MARK CROSSES THE NULL. At tau_int ~ 1.80 least squares reads a size of 1.04 with a spread
      of x2.9, so its bar runs 0.37 to 2.90: the typical direction is right while some directions are
      overstated and others understated at the same time. That mark alone is the argument for the
      whole size-and-shape decomposition, because no scalar summary can express it.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. tau_int is measured here as a median over 10 000 recordings per cell. An
experimenter has ONE, so the sampling distribution of tau_int at a single record is what fixes the
operational threshold and the false-alarm rate a reader would actually suffer. That analysis is
pending and the series is already emitted (Figure 3, row G), so it needs no run.

AND ONE CAUTION so the panel is not dismissed for the wrong reason. This project has recorded that
least squares' r^2_std of exactly 1 is a tautology, since the classical fit standardizes the residual
by a variance fitted to that same residual. That does NOT apply here: scaling a residual by a
constant leaves its autocorrelation unchanged, so tau_int is not self-referential.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# tau_int is a property of the LEAST-SQUARES residual and of nothing else: it is what the reader has
# before choosing a method, so it is the x of every mark including the filter's.
tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% c("nonlinearsqr", "macro_IR")) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(ifelse(algo == "nonlinearsqr", "ILSE", "IR"),
                         levels = c("ILSE", "IR")),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))))

cat(sprintf("figure_6B: %d marks, %d cells, intervals %s\n",
            nrow(dat), n_distinct(dat[c("noise","Num_ch","interval_in_tau")]),
            paste(levels(dat$d), collapse = " ")))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 3.6}
# The estimation floor of the shape statistic, drawn on the filter's side so a reader can see that
# its bars are the bootstrap and not a finding.
FLOOR <- 1.043

g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ member, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20),
                labels = c("1", "1.2", "1.5", "2", "3", "5", "10", "20")) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 200),
                labels = c("0.3", "0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "30", "100", "200")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(Delta*t %.% k[off]), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))

ggsave("Figure_6B.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 3.6, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
# the statements in the note, rebuilt from the data so the two cannot drift
dat %>% filter(member == "ILSE") %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(tau_int, c(0, 1.02, 1.5, 3, 6, 100))) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), size = median(mag), shape = median(aniso),
            lo = median(lo), hi = median(hi), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nIR over the whole sweep: size", sprintf("%.3f", median(dat$mag[dat$member == "IR"])),
    " shape", sprintf("%.3f", median(dat$aniso[dat$member == "IR"])),
    " (floor", FLOOR, ")\n")
```
